author: Matt Slick
title: What is the ultimate authority of the Eastern Orthodox & Catholic Churches?
text:
What is the ultimate authority in the Eastern Orthodox and Catholic Churches? It is not God’s word. In actuality, it is their churches. Both the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic churches claim to be the one true church with the authority to interpret God’s word. Of course, these two churches contradict each other in several areas, each claiming to be true. (They differ on the Pope, the filioque, the Immaculate Conception, Purgatory, and more). Nevertheless, what is the ultimate authority in these churches? It should be Scripture, but it isn’t. It is their own particular church.
Eastern Orthodoxy “It is from the Church that the Bible ultimately derives its authority, for it was the Church which originally decided which books form a part of Holy Scripture; and it is the Church alone which can interpret Holy Scripture with authority.” (Ware, Timothy. The Orthodox Church: An Introduction to Eastern Christianity (p. 193). Penguin Books Ltd. Kindle Edition, Timothy Ware is also known as Metropolitan Kallistos Ware). Roman Catholicism “The task of giving an authentic interpretation of the Word of God, whether in its written form or in the form of Tradition, has been entrusted to the living teaching office of the Church alone. Its authority in this matter is exercised in the name of Jesus Christ” (Catechism of the Catholic Church, 85). Whenever we have a church that is the final authority and not God’s word, then God’s word means whatever the church says it means. Of course, these churches claim apostolic authority and that they gave us the Scripture. They claim authenticity, finality, and truth. But their arguments are circular.
Each of these two churches claims to have given us the Bible. Yet the Bible gave us their churches. Each of these two churches claims to properly interpret God’s word. Yet each interprets God’s word to support their own church’s authority. I reject the authority of the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic churches for many reasons. They preach a false gospel, have a false priesthood, and promote idolatry. The Gospel they each preach is a combination of faith and works. The priesthood they have presents a special class of clergy, with special authority, and special garments, who work before an altar, and present sacrifices of the Eucharist. Each one promotes the idea that saints in heaven can hear millions of prayers simultaneously spoken and thought in different languages all over the earth and comprehend them. As a result, it’s okay to pray to them. This is idolatrous because it gives to the created beings the qualities that belong to God.
The Ultimate Authority Nevertheless, below I present an argument that the Scriptures are the final authority. in fact, they are the ultimate authority.
An ultimate is that which is nothing is equal or greater. Therefore by definition, there can only be one. If there were multiple ultimates, that would contradict what an ultimate is – nothing equal or greater. The Ultimate for Christians would be God Himself. He is the necessary and self-existent being (I AM who I AM, Exodus 3:14). There is nothing greater than Him and there’s nothing equal to Him (Isaiah 43:10; 44:6, 8; 45:5). We do not have a direct back-and-forth line to God with which we can ask questions and get direct, verbal answers. In lieu of that, God gave us His inspired word, the Scriptures. In the Garden of Adam and Eve, Genesis 2:17, God said, “But from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat from it you will surely die.” When God spoke to Adam, He gave him His direct word. This direct word from God is, by definition, inspired. It is God breathed. God’s direct word serves as the ultimate truth to which Adam was obligated to submit. This is because the word of God reflects God’s character. It represents Him. It comes from Him. In part, this is why God does not defend Himself or His Scripture. Because He is true and the final authority, His word is true and the final authority. Likewise, the Scriptures are God-breathed (2 Tim. 3:16). That which is inspired by God has the same level of authority as God’s direct word found in places like Gen. 2:17. Therefore, the Scriptures are the ultimate authority for us today in the true Christian Church. What I have provided is logically coherent. It is grounded biblically and follows logically. This is called a polysyllogism, a construction of statements that logically lead to the following statement until we arrive at a conclusion. Let me reduce the above nine statements into five.
From Nine to Five An ultimate is that which has nothing equal or greater, so by definition, there can only be one. For Christians, that Ultimate is God Himself, the necessary and self‑existent One (Exodus 3:14; Isaiah 45:5). Since we do not have direct back‑and‑forth communication with God, He has given us His inspired Word, the Scriptures. God’s direct Word, as given to Adam in Genesis 2:17, was inspired and carried ultimate authority because it reflects His character. Likewise, the Scriptures are God‑breathed (2 Timothy 3:16) and therefore serve as the ultimate authority for the true Christian Church today. From Five to Three Now I will reduce these 5 to 3. These are intended to help you think through these issues, one step at a time.
By definition, there can only be one Ultimate, and for Christians, that Ultimate is God, the self‑existent One (Exodus 3:14; Isaiah 45:5). Since we do not have direct communication with God, He has given us His inspired and God‑breathed Word, the Scriptures (2 Timothy 3:16). Because Scripture reflects God’s character and carries His authority, it is the final and ultimate authority for the Christian Church today.
Conclusion The Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches claim the Scriptures are inspired, yet make their own authority the ultimate standard, which alone has the right to interpret God’s Word. Both contradict each other on issues such as the papacy, the filioque, the Immaculate Conception, and purgatory. However, the Bible itself is God‑breathed (2 Timothy 3:16), reflecting His character and carrying His authority, making Scripture the true and ultimate authority for Christians.
